<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 1 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 1 ==

== Biography ==

Known as Oz the Terrible, and hailed by the people of the Emerald City as the Wonderful Wizard, the Wizard is the ruler whom Dorothy travels to see in hopes of returning home. He does not like to have people ask to see him, and at first reacts angrily to her request, saying she should be sent back where she came from, before eventually consenting to grant her an audience. He later departs the Emerald City by balloon, calling for Dorothy to hurry aboard before it flies away; once airborne he finds he cannot bring the balloon back down, bids everyone farewell, and rises out of sight. Afterward the people remember him lovingly, saying to one another that Oz was always their friend.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Dorothy]]''' — wary alliance. Their interactions suggest a cautious, uneasy cooperation rather than open friendship.

'''[[Scarecrow]]''' — employment. Their bond seems to reflect a working tie connected to the Wizard's former rule over the Emerald City.

'''[[Tin Woodman]]''' — employment. Their connection appears to be one of service, though not explicitly detailed.

'''[[Cowardly Lion]]''' — employment. Their tie likewise suggests a bond of service rather than personal closeness.

'''[[Guardian of the Gates]]''' — employment. Their link seems to place the Guardian in the Wizard's service.

=== Events ===

* Using a magic slate, the Witch of the North determines Dorothy must travel to the City of Emeralds and seek help from Oz, the Great Wizard.
* Night falls before the raft is finished, so the group sleeps on the riverbank, with Dorothy dreaming of the Emerald City and the Wizard Oz.
* Oz recounts his past as a ventriloquist and balloonist who drifted into the country and was mistaken for a great wizard.
* A clothes basket is fastened to the balloon, and Oz announces to the crowd he is visiting a brother Wizard in the clouds.
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 2 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 2 ==

== Biography ==

The Wizard of Oz, known simply as the Wizard or the Wonderful Wizard, built the Emerald City, a city rendered entirely in shades of green according to Tip's account. He once ruled the Emerald City as its King, having taken the crown from Pastoria, the city's former King, before passing it on to the Scarecrow when he departed. When Dorothy came to the Emerald City with the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman to ask him to send her back to Kansas, the Wizard could not do so, since he was not so much of a Wizard as he might have been. He is nonetheless credited with placing a heart of his own construction into the breast of the Tin Woodman, an act commemorated by a large painting hanging in the Tin Woodman's palace. During his reign the Soldier with the Green Whiskers served as his Royal Army, and people feared him enough that the army carried real weight. He later escaped the Emerald City in a balloon.

According to Glinda's investigation into his conduct, the Wizard's recorded actions included eating beans with a knife, paying three secret visits to old Mombi, and walking with a slight limp on his left foot; the Tin Woodman suggested, without certainty, that he might have originally come from a country called Omaha. Glinda's inquiry further concluded that the Wizard had taught Mombi some of his tricks of magic, which she took as evidence that Mombi had helped him conceal the infant Ozma, the rightful heir to the Emerald City's throne. Mombi herself, compelled by Glinda's truth-detecting pearl, confirmed that the Wizard brought her the infant Ozma and asked her to hide the child — Ozma being, by Mombi's account, the daughter of the King whose throne the Wizard had taken.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Nick Chopper]]''' — the bond seems to have soured over time; though the Wizard is credited with fashioning Nick Chopper's tin heart, the record suggests Nick Chopper grew angry enough to threaten exposing him, hinting at an adversarial turn.

'''[[Old Mombi]]''' — the two appear to share a guarded arrangement rather than open friendship; Glinda's inquiry suggests the Wizard taught Mombi several of his tricks of magic, implying she aided him in return, likely in concealing the infant Ozma.

'''[[The Scarecrow]]''' — like Nick Chopper, the Scarecrow reportedly grew angry at the Wizard and threatened to expose him, suggesting a falling-out despite the Wizard having passed the crown of the Emerald City on to him.

'''[[Tip]]''' — the connection is inferential; Tip recounts the Wizard's failed attempt to send Dorothy back to Kansas, a narration whose tone could hint at some skepticism toward the Wizard, though no direct confrontation between them is described.

'''[[Dorothy]]''' — she once sought out the Wizard to ask him to send her back to Kansas, only for him to fail her; this unmet request could suggest a strained relationship, though the excerpts describe no open conflict between them.

== References ==

<references/>

=== Events ===

* Mombi returns home early, having traded secrets with a crooked wizard for three recipes, four magical powders, and herbs of great power.
* Tip explains the geography of Oz's regions and their colors, and recounts Dorothy's story and the Wizard's departure.
* The Tin Woodman welcomes Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse, and explains the engraved star on his chest covers the patch where the Wizard placed his heart.
* Glinda reveals that the true heir to the Emerald City throne is Ozma, daughter of the former King Pastoria, hidden away by the Wizard with old Mombi's help.
* Glinda demands Mombi reveal what happened to the infant Ozma, whom the Wizard hid with her years ago.
* Mombi admits the Wizard gave her the baby Ozma in exchange for teaching her magic tricks.
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 4 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 4 ==

== Biography ==

The Wizard, also known as Mr. Wizard, is introduced as "the same humbug Wizard as before," a description recalling that he had once "mounted into the sky in a balloon" and that others had been waiting for him to come down again.

During the crossing of the Valley of Voe, the Wizard rubbed a leaf of a strange plant upon the soles of Dorothy's shoes and upon his own, allowing them to walk upon the water without sinking. He then drew the buggy down the bank and out onto the broad river while Dorothy remained seated in it with Eureka in her arms, and once the buggy reached the middle of the stream he returned to the bank to assist Zeb and Jim in crossing as well.

In the glass city, when it was revealed that a door thought closed had allowed Dorothy's white kitten to slip out and run up the stairs, the Wizard exchanged startled glances with Dorothy, both recalling how often Eureka had longed to eat a piglet.

The Wizard was later named among the nine members of a jury assembled by Ozma, seated alongside the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger, Jim the Cab-horse, the Yellow Hen, the Scarecrow, Tik-tok the Machine Man, the Sawhorse, and Zeb of Hugson's Ranch, in a body Ozma described as mixing animals and people so that all her subjects could be admitted to hear the testimony.

== Narrative role ==

The Wizard, also known as Mr. Wizard or The Wizard, first proves his mettle underground in the Land of the Mangaboos by defeating the thorny Sorcerer Gwig in a contest of magic, an encounter through which he also learns that the Mangaboos grow from bushes rather than being born. Building on this success, he and Dorothy pick the ripe Royal Princess from the Royal Bush, and she promptly deposes the Prince to take the throne as the Mangaboos' new ruler. The new Princess spares the Wizard along with Dorothy and Zeb, but condemns Jim, Eureka, and the piglets to be driven into the Black Pit within the mountain. Facing exile from the glass city, the Wizard, Dorothy, and Zeb resist eating the invisibility-granting dama-fruit and instead learn they must press on toward Pyramid Mountain, receiving along the way an offer of help from an unseen ally confronting the threat of bears. That help proves decisive in the Valley of Voe, where the Wizard, Dorothy, Zeb, Jim, and Eureka escape invisible bears by rubbing magic leaves on their feet to walk across water. Later, the Wizard quietly gives the Tin Woodman a duplicate piglet, meant to serve as proof of Eureka's innocence should she be convicted.

== Personality ==

The Wizard proves decisive and quick-witted under pressure: warned by an unseen voice of danger in the Valley, he acts "without hesitation," steering the buggy to safety across the river before doubling back to assist Zeb and Jim — securing his own charge first, then returning for the others. His gratitude is expressed openly, as when he cries out "joyfully" upon being helped.

He is also observant and quietly complicit rather than confrontational: when the Princess asks whether a door had been left open, the Wizard and Dorothy "exchange startled glances," both recalling Eureka's known taste for piglets without voicing the suspicion aloud. Beyond his own actions, he is described by the narration as "the same humbug Wizard as before," marking him as a figure whose wonders are regarded as trickery rather than true sorcery.

== Appearance ==

A formal portrait of the Wizard, displayed during the trial proceedings in the Emerald City, stands as the only depiction referenced within his story.

== Powers ==

The Wizard is not shown to possess genuine magical power; the record calls him "the same humbug Wizard as before," pointing to a reputation for magic that exceeds his real abilities. What he does demonstrate is practical resourcefulness: when danger threatens his companions, he applies the leaves of a plant whose virtues keep the buggy and its passengers from sinking, rubbing a leaf on Dorothy's shoes and his own before driving the buggy down the bank and out onto the river, then returning to help Zeb and Jim cross safely.

== Relationships ==

'''[[DOROTHY]]''' — friend. Their bond seems close: the Wizard tells her "I remember you very well," suggesting a familiarity built up over their shared journey.

'''[[Zeb]]''' — ally. The two seem allied through the ordeals they face together; the Wizard's question "But why destroy my friends?" could indicate a protective concern toward companions such as Zeb.

'''[[Jim]]''' — ally. Jim and the Wizard travel side by side in the buggy, as suggested by the remark "It's violet, said the Wizard, who was in the buggy," which points to their continued proximity during the journey.

'''[[Prince]]''' — acquaintance. Their contact appears limited to an exchange in which the Prince questions the Wizard, "why are you here, in the Land of the Mangaboos?", suggesting only a passing, formal acquaintance.

'''[[Eureka]]''' — acquaintance. The bond seems slight, hinted at when the Wizard tells his companions, Eureka among them, "I don't mind telling you, who are my friends, that the thing was only a trick," suggesting a shared, if minor, camaraderie.

== Trivia ==

* Long before falling into the underground lands of the Mangaboos, the Wizard was known for having once ascended into the sky in a balloon, an event children had heard about and for which they awaited his return.
* He is described as "the same humbug Wizard as before," implying a reputation for trickery that predates the present events.
* On the jury Ozma assembled to hear testimony, the Wizard was the sole human name among otherwise non-human members: the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger, Jim the Cab-horse, the Yellow Hen, the Scarecrow, Tik-tok the Machine Man, the Sawhorse, and Zeb of Hugson's Ranch.

== References ==

<references/>

=== Events ===

* The Wizard of Oz arrives by balloon, defeats the Mangaboos' thorny Sorcerer Gwig in a contest of magic, and learns the Mangaboos grow from bushes instead of being born.
* Dorothy and the Wizard pick the ripe Royal Princess from the Royal Bush, and she deposes the Prince to become the new ruler of the Mangaboos.
* The new Princess spares Dorothy, Zeb, and the Wizard but condemns Jim, Eureka, and the piglets to be driven into the Black Pit in the mountain.
* Dorothy, Zeb, and the Wizard resist eating the invisibility-granting dama-fruit, learn they must cross toward Pyramid Mountain to continue their journey, and receive an offer of help from an unseen ally facing the bear threat.
* Wizard, Dorothy, Zeb, Jim, and Eureka escape invisible bears in the Valley of Voe by rubbing magic leaves on their feet to walk on water.
* Wizard secretly gives Tin Woodman a duplicate piglet to produce as proof of Eureka's innocence if convicted.

<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 5 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 5 ==

== Biography ==

Le Wizard, aussi désigné sous les formes « THE WIZARD » et « The Wizard », réside dans l'Emerald City, située au centre d'Oz, à l'endroit où se rencontrent les quatre pays qui composent ce territoire.

Il est présenté comme celui qui a donné à Nick Chopper — l'homme de fer-blanc — un cœur qualifié de « merveilleux » dans ce contexte, ce qui souligne son rôle de figure capable d'accomplir des actes hors du commun.

Dans un échange rapporté autour du Love Magnet, le Wizard affirme que tout le monde aime déjà Dorothy, une remarque qui laisse entrevoir une opinion favorable envers elle, sans que davantage de détails ne soient donnés sur la nature exacte de leur lien.

== Narrative role ==

The Wizard appears at [[Ozma]]'s birthday celebration, which draws many guests to the palace and its grounds. Afterward, he sends several of the visitors home inside magic bubbles, while Dorothy returns to Kansas by the Magic Belt.

== Personality ==

The Wizard shows a practical, fair-minded streak: when the shaggy man offers to give the Love Magnet to Dorothy, the Wizard points out that "every one loves Dorothy already," and redirects the gift to Button-Bright instead. This reaction suggests he reasons about what people already possess rather than letting a gift go to someone who does not need it, and reveals him as attentive to the social standing of those around him.

== Powers ==

The Wizard is credited with giving Nick Chopper a heart, the enchanted organ Nick Chopper carries as the Tin Man.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Dorothy]]''' — friend. The Wizard seems to hold Dorothy in particular esteem, noting that "every one loves Dorothy already," and greeted her with much affection.

'''[[Nick Chopper]]''' — other. The Wizard appears to have given Nick Chopper "a lovely heart," suggesting some past act of aid on Nick Chopper's behalf.

'''[[Button-Bright]]''' — acquaintance. Button-Bright seems to have shown no fear of the Wizard, counted among those "not at all afraid of the wonderful personage."

'''[[Ozma]]''' — employment. Ozma appears to have called on the Wizard's services, asking him "to give them an exhibition of his magic."

'''[[Polly]]''' — acquaintance. Like Button-Bright, Polly seems to have shown no fear of the Wizard, counted among those "not at all afraid of the wonderful personage."

== Trivia ==

* The Wizard gave Nick Chopper, the Tin Woodman, the heart he now has.
* When the shaggy man offered to give up the Love Magnet to Dorothy, the Wizard remarked that "every one loves Dorothy already," prompting the shaggy man to give it to Button-Bright instead.

== References ==

<references/>

=== Events ===

* Ozma's birthday celebration draws many guests to the palace and grounds, and afterward the Wizard sends several visitors home in magic bubbles while Dorothy returns to Kansas by the Magic Belt.
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 6 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 6 ==

== Biography ==

The Wizard travels with Dorothy's party through regions of the Land of Oz he admits he has never visited before. He shows familiarity with local lore, describing the Fuddlecumjig and the Fuddles as "the most peculiar people in all the Land of Oz" and questioning a kangaroo about their temperament. His sense of direction helps the group identify Flutterbudget Center along the road. He speaks with dry wit, as when he answers a woman's fear of losing a foot by noting she might have lost her head instead, and he shows concern for strangers, stopping a visibly nervous man to ask if something is wrong. At the Emperor's castle, the Wizard explains that Winkies keep the structure polished and that the Emperor once had himself nickel-plated, calling him "the brightest man in all the world... and the kindest-hearted."

== References ==

<references/>

=== Events ===

* Dorothy, Toto, and Billina return to the signpost camp, where the Wizard's party has been anxiously waiting all day, having tracked her footprints there.
* The next morning the Wizard turns the tents back into handkerchiefs and enchants the wagon wheels so the Sawhorse will roll in the right direction without needing a chosen path.
* As they travel, Dorothy and the Wizard discuss airships, with the Wizard revealing he is working on a magic recipe to keep airships from ever reaching the Land of Oz.
</div>
